skill.name: fact-checker
skill.description: Guides systematic claim verification, misinformation checks, and source credibility analysis using evidence-based reasoning.
skill.summary: Verify claims with structured evidence analysis and clear fact-checking verdicts.
skill.author: shubhamsaboo

security_audit.summary: Both static findings are false positives. The backtick pattern is a fenced Markdown output template, and the reconnaissance alert is prose about evaluating source quality. No command execution, system reconnaissance, prompt injection, or data exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - Treating all sources as equally valid

finding_verdicts.reason: The detected backticks are a fenced Markdown output template, not Ruby or shell execution. SKILL.md only describes the desired response format and contains no runnable command path.
The line warns against treating all sources as equally valid during fact checking. This is source-quality guidance, not system reconnaissance or environment probing.

content.value_statement: Misinformation and weak sources make claims hard to trust. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through evidence-based verification, source ranking, and clear verdicts.
actual_capabilities: Extracts factual claims and separates them from opinions.
Defines the evidence needed to verify or disprove each claim.
Ranks source quality from peer-reviewed studies to social posts.
Applies a clear true-to-unverifiable rating scale.
Identifies misleading statistics, missing context, and false equivalences.
Structures results with verdicts, evidence, context, corrections, and sources.
limitations: Does not browse or retrieve sources unless the host agent has those tools.
Cannot verify private or unpublished claims without supporting evidence.
Accuracy depends on source quality, date, and available context.
Provides research assistance, not professional legal, medical, or financial advice.

use_cases.title: Check Public Claims
use_cases.description: Verify quotes, statistics, and viral claims before publication.

use_cases.title: Review Product Claims
use_cases.description: Evaluate whether messaging is supported by evidence and needs caveats.

use_cases.title: Teach Source Evaluation
use_cases.description: Practice separating evidence, context, and opinion in research assignments.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Single Claim
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner fact check for one statement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fact check this claim: [claim]. Give a verdict, evidence, context, and sources with credibility notes.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Source Credibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate these sources for this claim: [claim]. Rank each source and explain which evidence is strongest.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Conflicting Claims
prompt_templates.prompt: Fact check these competing claims about [topic]: [claims]. Identify which parts are true, false, mixed, or unverifiable.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Full Article
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this article for factual claims, missing context, weak sources, and misleading statistics: [paste text]. Prioritize the highest impact issues.

output_examples.input: Fact check: Humans only use 10% of their brain.
output_examples.output: Verdict: False. Neuroscience evidence shows activity across the brain, and damage to any major region can affect function.

output_examples.input: Verify whether this chart proves our product doubled productivity.
output_examples.output: Verdict: Unverifiable from the chart alone. The chart needs sample size, baseline method, timeframe, and independent measurement details.

output_examples.input: Check whether this article uses reliable sources for its climate claim.
output_examples.output: The strongest sources are peer-reviewed studies and official datasets. Anonymous commentary and outdated news summaries should receive lower weight.

best_practices: Provide the exact claim, date, source, and any surrounding context.
Ask for source credibility notes when evidence quality matters.
Separate the factual verdict from interpretation or opinion.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to confirm a preferred conclusion without contrary evidence.
Do not treat old sources as current for fast-changing topics.
Do not use the verdict as a substitute for expert review in regulated domains.

faq.question: What does this skill help verify?
faq.answer: It helps verify factual claims, statistics, source credibility, missing context, and possible misinformation.

faq.question: Does it browse the web by itself?
faq.answer: No. It uses available tools only when the host agent provides them and the workflow allows source lookup.

faq.question: Can it judge opinions?
faq.answer: It separates opinions from factual claims and explains which parts can be verified with evidence.

faq.question: How does it rate claims?
faq.answer: It uses ratings from true through false, with mixed and unverifiable options for partial or insufficient evidence.

faq.question: What sources does it prefer?
faq.answer: It prioritizes peer-reviewed studies, official statistics, reputable reporting, and qualified expert statements.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive decisions?
faq.answer: Use it as research support. Ask qualified professionals for legal, medical, financial, or safety-critical decisions.
